import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_18/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_18/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source2_18_0 and Source2_18_1 on 'city'
# According to intermediate_step1, only columns city, fare, ride_id are kept after join
# So we join on city, but only keep city, fare, ride_id from Source2_18_0 (since Source2_18_1 columns are not needed)
# The join is inner join by default to keep only matching cities
df_joined = pd.merge(df0[['city', 'fare', 'ride_id']], df1[['city']], on='city', how='inner')

# Operation 2: GROUP BY city, aggregations: avg(fare), max(ride_id)
df_grouped = df_joined.groupby('city', as_index=False).agg({
    'fare': 'mean',
    'ride_id': 'max'
})

# Ensure column types match target schema:
# city: string (already string)
# fare: float (mean aggregation produces float)
# ride_id: integer (max aggregation produces int64 or int64-compatible)
df_grouped['fare'] = df_grouped['fare'].astype(float)
df_grouped['ride_id'] = df_grouped['ride_id'].astype(int)

# Rename columns if needed (already matching target schema)
Target2_18 = df_grouped[['city', 'fare', 'ride_id']]

# Write to target path
Target2_18.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_18/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_18/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on city (inner join to avoid extra rows)

    "fare": "mean",
    "ride_id": "max"
})

# Ensure column order and names exactly as target schema
